newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Well supported by firm swaps.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Well supported by firm swaps.

text.p: Firm fuel oil swaps supported sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Wednesday and traders expected prices to stay at around current levels in the near term.
"Supplies from the Middle East should get tighter starting the second half of this month, so we can expect fuel oil prices to stay firm from now on," said one trader.
The market has been expecting fewer cargoes coming from Kuwait due to seasonal summer demand there, tightening supplies to Asia.
"Demand is not significant at the moment, but the expected tighter supplies will support prices," the trader said.
May fuel oil swaps were at $100.00/$101.00 against Tuesday's $100.25/$101.00. June swaps were at $98.50/$99.50 against $98.75/$99.50.
On Tuesday, a 180-cst grade, 20,000-tonne cargo was traded between two European majors at $100 per tonne for May 29-June 2 loading.
Sentiment was sluggish on SIMEX fuel oil futures contract on late Wednesday, with June contract unchanged at $99.50 while July was down 40 cents to $98.80.
Market focus was on two Taiwan fuel oil tenders.
Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp is expected to annouce the result on Thursday for a tender for two 0.5-percent, 38,000-tonne cargoes for June delivery.
CPC on Wednesday issued a tender to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil for June 2-27 lifting from Kaohsiung on a free-on-board (fob) basis.
The tender closes on May 14 and is valid until May 16.
